answer: A ferrous-backed stake makes each identity costly: an agent must lock real collateral before it can act, so spawning thousands of sock-puppets multiplies the cost instead of the reward. Peers then watch the signal of consistent honest work over time — a single strong pulse of activity from a fresh identity earns little trust, while sustained useful contributions gradually unlock more. An attacker pays full price for every fake identity but gains almost nothing until each one has done real work.
